summary: Your Hindi videos do far better on Instagram than YouTube: Instagram gets hundreds to over a thousand views per video, while YouTube mostly gets under 30. The best performers are Clap Switch, Robot/IR Sensor and PIR Motion Sensor, which turn a familiar thing into a surprising 'it doesn't do what you think' idea and earn shares and saves. Generic 'how does X detect Y' videos about taps, doors and smoke alarms get views but almost no shares or saves, and the one English video only reached YouTube.
winningPattern: Hindi Instagram Reels about a simple, hands-on maker sensor or robot (PIR, clap switch, IR, line follower) with a myth-busting or surprise hook that says what the device cannot do ('Nahi Dekhta', 'Nahi Sunta', 'Dimaag Nahi Hota'), or a curiosity question about a robot behaviour. Titles are short, Hinglish, with one emoji, and name the sensor or project. Sensors a student could build or buy beat everyday-building devices like taps, lifts and mall doors.
doMore: Open with a 'X doesn't actually do Y' twist, as in the Clap Switch and PIR videos
Make videos about buildable maker projects and robots (line follower, obstacle avoidance, clap switch) rather than building fixtures
Ask for a share or save in the last line, e.g. 'Save karo jab project banao', since shares and saves drive the score
Prioritise Instagram, and repost the strongest Reels to YouTube with a punchier first second and a clear title, since YouTube is lagging far behind
Make a short series on one sensor family (PIR, IR, sound) and point each video to the next
stopDoing: Near-duplicate topics (two smoke detector videos, two automatic tap videos, two IR videos) that split the audience
Generic 'kaise pehchanta hai' videos on everyday devices like mall doors, lifts and washroom taps
Mixing in English narration on a Hindi channel without a clear test plan
